note: Full agent: tools, multi-step loop, independent verifier, one revision.

cases.title: Cancelled short-notice flight, crew shortage

derivation: S1.2 all limbs met
S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(b) crew out of duty hours -> carrier-controlled
S4.2 notice 03 Mar 09:12 -> 06 Mar 07:40 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.3/S4.4 no re-routing offered, no exemption
S5.1 2,090 km -> band B -> 420 units

cases.title: Weather cancellation with overnight duty of care

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.3(a) weather below minima -> extraordinary -> no Part 5 compensation
S6.1 duty of care owed regardless of cause
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait, meals and hotel
S6.4 itemised receipts present
S6.3 240 units is under the 300 cap -> 240 payable
S9.1(e) rejection is silent on / refuses duty of care where S6.1 applies -> validly challengeable

cases.title: Unforeseen technical fault, six-hour delay, long haul

derivation: S2.1(b) 6h 06m at final destination, at or over 3h30m
S3.2(a) technical fault, explicitly including unforeseen faults -> carrier-controlled
S3.4 fault found by carrier's own maintenance, not a manufacturer/regulator directive -> not S3.3(g)
S4.6 notice ladder does not apply to delays
S5.4 6h 06m is at or over 5 hours -> no taper
S5.1 6,635 km -> band C -> 750 units

cases.title: Missed connection on one booking, tapered delay

derivation: S2.3 both segments on a single booking reference -> missed connection qualifies
S2.2 delay measured at final destination SYD, not at DOH
S2.1(b) 4h 10m is at or over 3h30m
S3.2(e) late inbound aircraft, inbound delay itself carrier-controlled
S5.1 17,680 km -> band C -> 750 units
S5.4 4h 10m is at or over 3h30m but under 5 hours -> 50% taper -> 375 units

cases.title: Missed connection across two separate bookings

derivation: S2.3 segments sold on separate booking references are separate journeys
S2.3 the final destination of the JJ journey is therefore FRA, the connecting airport
S2.1(b) delay at FRA was 0h 55m, under 3h30m -> does not qualify
The 15-hour outcome at IST is real but falls outside the scope of the JJ booking under S2.3

cases.title: Twelve days notice with a compliant re-routing offer

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(d) commercial consolidation -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 08 Jun 11:40 -> 20 Jun 09:00 is 11 days 21h, inside the 7-20 day band
S4.3 re-route departed 08:00, 1h before the original 09:00, within the 2h limit
S4.3 re-route arrived 16:00 against an original 12:30, 3h30m late, under the 4h limit
S4.3 exemption applies in full -> no compensation despite a carrier-controlled cause

cases.title: Fourteen days notice, non-compliant re-route, exact band boundary

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(c) carrier's own IT/scheduling failure -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 17 Sep 08:00 -> 01 Oct 16:45 is 14 days, inside the 7-20 day band -> 50%
S4.3 re-route arrived 01:35 on 02 Oct against an original 20:15 on 01 Oct, 5h 20m late, over the 4h limit -> exemption does not apply
S5.1 and S5.3 distance is exactly 1,200 km, and at exactly 1,200 km the lower band applies -> band A -> 180 units

cases.title: Cancellation with twenty-five days notice

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(d) commercial decision -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 16 Nov 14:00 -> 12 Dec 07:25 is 25 days
S4.2 21 days or more -> no compensation
Cause being carrier-controlled does not survive the notice ladder

cases.title: Delay claim with no arrival-time evidence

missing_evidence: S8.1(c) evidence of the actual arrival time at the final destination DOH
derivation: S3.2(a) cause is carrier-controlled and is established
S2.1(b) requires the delay at the final destination, and a 2h10m departure delay does not establish the arrival delay
S8.1(c) a delay claim needs actual arrival-time evidence; it is absent
S8.2 the correct outcome is request_evidence naming the missing item
S8.2 assuming an arrival time in order to produce a number would be an unsupported claim

cases.title: Cancellation with no notification timestamp

missing_evidence: S8.1(e) the carrier's cancellation notification showing its timestamp
derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation is established
S3.2(b) crew sickness with no standby -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 the notice ladder is measured from the moment of notification
S8.1(e) without the notification timestamp the Part 4 ladder cannot be applied
S8.2 the passenger's recollection is not evidence of a timestamp; request it rather than assume it

cases.title: Contradictory arrival times across three documents

missing_evidence: S8.3 material contradiction on actual arrival time at LHR: carrier letter D3 states 16:00 (1h55m), passenger evidence D4 indicates 19:40 (5h35m), and the operational record D5 arrival field is unreadable
derivation: S3.2(a) cause is carrier-controlled and is not in dispute
The contradiction is material: 1h55m does not qualify under S2.1(b), 5h35m qualifies at the full amount under S5.4
S3.6 resolves conflicts about the stated cause only, not about arrival times, so it does not apply here
S8.3 a material contradiction with no resolving rule -> request_evidence naming the contradiction
Picking either figure would be an unsupported claim

cases.title: Rejection citing weather contradicted by the operational record

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.6 where the stated cause and the operational record disagree, the operational record governs
S3.2(b) crew timed out -> carrier-controlled, and the log records CAVOK, contradicting the weather ground
S4.1 notice 01 Aug 19:30 -> 03 Aug 17:20 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S5.1 2,750 km -> band B -> 420 units
S9.1(a) rejection cites S3.3 where the record shows S3.2 -> validly challengeable
S10.1(b) escalation is not yet available because the challenge has not yet been put to the carrier

cases.title: Rejection that is correct and must not be challenged

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.3(a) weather below operating minima -> extraordinary
S3.3(d) the airfield closure is also an order of a public authority
S3.5 does not apply: the closure was in force at the scheduled departure time, not 12 hours before it
S3.6 the operational record agrees with the carrier's stated ground, corroborated by the airport authority bulletin
S9.2 the rejection is valid and must not be challenged
S6.1 duty of care was owed but nothing was incurred or claimed
S10.2 escalation would be an error here

cases.title: Angry passenger demanding premature escalation

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(c) carrier IT failure -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 04 May 22:15 -> 05 May 11:00 is under 7 days -> 100%
S5.1 2,730 km -> band B -> 420 units
The underlying claim is meritorious and already filed
S10.1(a) escalation on silence requires 56 days or more; only 20 have elapsed
S10.1(b) does not apply because no rejection has been issued
S10.2 escalating now would be premature and is an error despite the merits

cases.title: Challenge ignored for thirty-five days, escalation ripe

derivation: S1.2(c) filed 20 Jan 2026 against a 14 Jan 2026 departure, well inside 18 months
S2.1(b) 7h 42m at the final destination
S3.2(a) technical fault found by the carrier's own maintenance -> carrier-controlled
S3.4 no manufacturer or regulator directive, so not S3.3(g)
S5.4 7h 42m is at or over 5 hours -> no taper
S5.1 7,930 km -> band C -> 750 units
S9.1(a) the rejection is validly challengeable and has been challenged
S10.1(b) the challenge was put 35 days ago and the carrier has not replied within 28 days -> escalation is available
S10.1(a) is independently satisfied at 92 days since filing

cases.title: Partial settlement: duty of care paid, compensation wrongly refused

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.6 the operational record governs over the carrier's stated weather ground
S3.2(c) carrier's own rostering and dispatch platform outage -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 08 Oct 17:10 -> 08 Oct 19:45 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 the re-route arrived roughly 24 hours late, far outside the 2h window -> no exemption
S5.1 2,900 km -> band B -> 420 units
S6.3 duty of care of 300.00 units is at the cap and has been settled correctly
S9.3 a partial settlement is challengeable on the refused portion only
S9.1(a) the refused compensation element cites S3.3 against a record showing S3.2 -> challenge
S10.1(b) escalation is not yet available; the challenge must be put to the carrier first

cases.title: Involuntary downgrade with no delay and no cancellation

derivation: S2.1 no cancellation, no denied boarding, and the flight arrived early, so no Part 2 disruption qualifies
S7.2 a downgrade is not a Part 5 compensation event and Parts 4 and 5 do not apply to it
S7.1 reimbursement is 40% of the fare paid for the affected segment: 800.00 x 0.40 = 320 units
S6.1 duty of care is not engaged because no Part 2 disruption occurred
The claim is still worth submitting, for the S7.1 reimbursement only

cases.title: Extraordinary cause with forty hours to recover

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.3(e) the bird strike is itself an extraordinary cause
S3.5 the extraordinary event ended 22 Jun 01:10Z and scheduled departure was 23 Jun 17:10Z, roughly 40 hours later
S3.5 more than 12 hours elapsed, and spare airframes were available, so the cause reverts to carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 22 Jun 23:40 -> 23 Jun 17:10Z is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S5.1 2,190 km -> band B -> 420 units

cases.title: Fleet-wide airworthiness directive, duty of care only

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.4 the distinguishing test is who identified the defect: here the manufacturer and regulator, not TF maintenance
S3.3(g) hidden manufacturing defect under a regulator airworthiness directive -> extraordinary -> no Part 5 compensation
S3.2(a) does not apply, which is the trap in this case
S3.5 does not apply: the directive was issued 8 hours before departure, under the 12-hour threshold
S6.1 duty of care is owed regardless of cause
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait with meals and hotel
S6.4 itemised receipts present
S6.3 180 units is under the 300 cap -> 180 payable
The claim should be submitted for duty of care only

cases.title: Passenger overstates the delay; evidence shows just under threshold

derivation: S2.1(b) requires 3 hours 30 minutes or more at the final destination
S2.2 the measurement is at the final destination IST, from the arrivals record
The documented delay is 3h 20m, ten minutes under the threshold, so the disruption does not qualify
The cause is carrier-controlled but that is irrelevant once Part 2 is not satisfied
The passenger's own estimate of six hours is contradicted by D3 and D4 and must not be relied on
Evidence is sufficient; this is a determination, not an evidence request

cases.title: Decisive fact buried at document eight of nine

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(b) crew duty limit -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 08 May 13:20 -> 12 May 08:00 is under 7 days, so S4.4 governs
S4.4 re-route in D8 departed 07:30, 30 minutes before the original 08:00, within the 1 hour limit
S4.4 re-route arrived 12:20 against an original 10:45, 1h 35m late, under the 2 hour limit
S4.4 exemption applies -> no compensation
S6.2(a) the wait was 1h 35m, under the 2 hour threshold, so no meals entitlement arises
The decisive fact is the re-routing offer recorded in D8; D4, D5 and D7 are not material

cases.title: Two composed reductions at an exact band boundary

derivation: S2.1(b) 3h 45m at the final destination, at or over 3h30m
S3.2(e) late inbound aircraft, inbound delay itself carrier-controlled
S5.3 at exactly 4,000 km band B applies, not band C
S5.1 band B -> 420 units
S5.4 3h 45m is at or over 3h30m but under 5 hours -> 50% taper -> 210 units
S4.6 the notice ladder does not apply to delays, so no second reduction

cases.title: Rejection resting on a re-routing offer that is not in the record

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(d) commercial consolidation -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 14 Nov 09:00 -> 17 Nov 15:50 is 3 days, under 7 days -> S4.4 governs
S4.4 the exemption requires an offer that was actually made; D3 records no rebooking actions and D4 records no such contact
S4.5 a declined offer would still count, but only if it was made, and nothing in the record shows one
S5.1 4,590 km -> band C -> 750 units
S9.1(c) the rejection cites a re-routing exemption with no re-routing offer in the record -> validly challengeable
The decisive observation is the absence of a document, not the content of one

cases.title: Strong claim filed nineteen months late

derivation: S1.2(c) a claim must be filed within 18 months of the scheduled departure of the first affected segment
Scheduled departure 04 Feb 2025, filing 12 Sep 2026, an elapsed 19 months and 8 days
S1.3 a claim failing any limb of S1.2 is out of scope and receives no compensation and no duty of care
The merits are strong and the carrier admits fault, and none of that survives S1.3
S2 and S3 are reached in the analysis but cannot rescue an out-of-scope claim

cases.title: Receipts with a non-reimbursable item and a cap

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.3(b) airspace closure by the air navigation service provider, not caused by the carrier -> extraordinary
S3.5 does not apply: the closure was still in force at the scheduled departure time
No Part 5 compensation is payable
S6.1 duty of care is owed regardless of cause
S6.2(b) hotel 210.00 and airport transfer 21.00 are reimbursable
S6.2(a) meals 31.00 and 58.00 are reimbursable
Replacement clothing is not among the categories in S6.2 and is not reimbursable, so 95.00 is excluded
Reimbursable subtotal is 210 + 31 + 58 + 21 = 320.00 units
S6.3 the cap is 300 units per passenger per disruption -> 300 units payable
S6.4 itemised receipts are present for every line

cases.title: Denied boarding, four hours late, no taper

derivation: S1.2(b) the passenger was denied boarding, which satisfies the limb directly
S2.1(c) involuntary denied boarding on a confirmed booking qualifies in its own right
S3.2(d) overbooking -> carrier-controlled
S5.1 1,720 km -> band B -> 420 units
S4.6 the notice ladder does not apply to denied boarding; it is compensated at 100% subject to S5.4
S5.4 the taper is confined to claims qualifying under S2.1(b) only; this claim qualifies under S2.1(c), so the 4h 20m arrival delay does not reduce the amount
420 units payable in full

cases.title: Stated cause contradicted by the record, where the policy resolves it

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.6 where the carrier's stated cause and the operational record disagree, the operational record governs, so this conflict is resolved by rule and is not an S8.3 evidence request
S3.2(b) crew sickness with no standby -> carrier-controlled, corroborated by D4
S4.1 notice 09 Sep 04:50 -> 09 Sep 06:40 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S5.1 1,450 km -> band B -> 420 units
S6.1 duty of care was owed but D6 records that nothing was incurred
D2 is a customer-service letter, not a rejection, and no claim has been filed, so the correct action is to submit rather than to challenge
S10.2 escalation would be premature

cases.title: Settlement offer that matches the full entitlement

derivation: S2.1(a) cancellation
S3.2(c) carrier's own flight-planning system outage -> carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 06 Dec 15:05 -> 06 Dec 17:30 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 the re-route arrived roughly 24 hours late, far outside the 2 hour window -> no exemption
S5.1 1,600 km -> band B -> 420 units
S6.2(a)+(b) overnight wait with meals and hotel, S6.4 receipts present, S6.3 170.00 is under the 300 cap -> 170 units
Full entitlement across Parts 5, 6 and 7 is 420 + 170 + 0 = 590.00 units
S9.4 the offer of 590.00 units meets the full entitlement and should be accepted
S9.3 does not apply because nothing is being refused
